front: What is d/dx[sin(f(x))] using the chain rule?
What is d/dx[cos(f(x))] using the chain rule?

back: Apply the chain rule: derivative of sin(f(x)) is f′(x)cos(f(x)). Here f(x)=3x²+1, so f′(x)=6x. Result: 6x cos(3x²+1)

front: State the product rule for differentiating h(x) = f(x)g(x)
State the quotient rule for differentiating h(x) = f(x)/g(x)
Find d/dx[x²sin(x)] and express in factorised form
back: Apply the product rule with f(x)=x², g(x)=sin(x): f′(x)=2x, g′(x)=cos(x). Result: 2x sin(x) + x²cos(x), factorised as x(2sin(x) + x cos(x))
